metadata.title: Towards Communication Efficient Multi-Agent Cooperations: Reinforcement Learning and LLM
metadata.abstract_summary: Combines reinforcement learning and LLM agents so that robots broadcast only a few human-readable features under a hard bandwidth budget, cutting message size by about 60% at equal reward in simulation.

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
What the paper proposes or defines, as extracted (section, page):
- **Coverage-collision objective** (category A) - Task metric combining landmark coverage distance and collision counts, weighted by eta, used as the reward for both communication and navigation policies. (section D. Problem Formulation, p. 5)
  > This term sums the distances between each landmark and its closest robot.
- **Goal-oriented interpretable feature protocol** (category D) - Robots broadcast only selected, human-readable observation features (velocity, own position, landmark positions) instead of opaque embeddings, so untrained agents can interpret messages. (section B. Goal-Oriented Human-Interpretable Feature Communication, p. 4)
  > we introduce a novel selective feature communication mechanism that allows robots to broadcast only the most important features
- **Alternating dual-policy optimization** (category B) - Deployment schema splitting orchestration into a communication policy and a navigation policy, optimized alternately while each conditions on the other. (section A. Alternating Dual-Policy Optimization, p. 5)
  > one policy is held ﬁxed while the other is optimized iteratively
- **Constrained MAPPO feature selection** (category D) - Lagrangian primal-dual MAPPO that learns per-feature transmit decisions under a hard bandwidth budget, with adaptive penalty on message size. (section B. Constrained MAPPO-Based Feature Communication Policy, p. 7)
  > λi is a penalty coefﬁcient that adjusts the impact of communication costs on the reward.

  > The Feature Ranking Agent evaluates and prioritizes the observed features based on their importance

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Coverage-collision objective**: Ct = Σ_{m=1}^{M} min_{i∈N} ||u^i_t − ũ^m||; Pt = Σ_{i=1}^{N−1} Σ_{k=i+1}^{N} I(||u^i_t − u^k_t|| < dmin); minimize E[Σ_{t=0}^{∞} γ^t(Ct + ηPt)] subject to S(m^i_t) ≤ B^i_t.
- **Goal-oriented interpretable feature protocol**: Binary selection vector g^i_t with g^{i,k}_t ∈ {0,1}; message m^i_t = {o^{i,k}_t | k ∈ K^i_t}; size S(m^i_t) = Σ_{k∈K^i_t} S(o^{i,k}_t) must satisfy S(m^i_t) ≤ B^i_t.
- **Alternating dual-policy optimization**: Algorithm 1: hold one policy fixed, optimize the other; communication phase minimizes L(ϕ), maximizes L(φi), updates λi; action phase minimizes L(ϑ), maximizes L(θi); then switch optimization phase.
- **Constrained MAPPO feature selection**: rcom_t = −(Ct + ηPt) − λiS(m^i_t); λi ← Γλ(λi + αλ(S(m^i_t) − B^i_t)); actor maximizes clipped PPO objective with entropy σH[ρi]; advantage via GAE.
- **LLM-BDP four-agent decomposition**: Feature Ranking outputs reasoning plus ranked features; Bandwidth Adaptive picks the maximum transmissible subset; Navigation proposes candidate actions toward a target; Collision Avoidance selects the lowest-risk action. Prompt edits adapt bandwidth without retraining.
- **Contextual memory and few-shot agent schema**: Contextual memory stores past observations and actions for refining later decisions; few-shot examples demonstrate reasoning steps; output expectations require a reasoning process followed by the ranked list, reducing hallucination.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Evidence the authors report:
  - Coverage-collision objective: Navigation reward curves over 25-step episodes with three robots and three landmarks compare MAPPO-BDP against MAPPO-NC, MAPPO-RS, MAPPO-CS, MAPPO-FC.
  - Goal-oriented interpretable feature protocol: Hybrid episode: robots 1-2 run MAPPO-BDP, robot 3 runs LLM-BDP-GMF; robot 3 interprets messages and completes the task without co-training.
  - Alternating dual-policy optimization: MAPPO-BDP with Wc = 1 kHz attains the highest convergence navigation reward among MAPPO-NC, MAPPO-RS and MAPPO-CS baselines.
  - Constrained MAPPO feature selection: At 2 kHz, MAPPO-BDP matches MAPPO-FC navigation reward while average message size drops from 80 bytes to about 32 bytes, a 60% reduction.
  - LLM-BDP four-agent decomposition: LLM-BDP-GZ finishes coverage in 10 steps; gpt-4o zero-shot beats gpt-4o-mini; few-shot prompts rescue gpt-4o-mini, which fails zero-shot.
  - Contextual memory and few-shot agent schema: Few-shot gpt-4o-mini (LLM-BDP-GMF) completes the task and preferentially selects position feature F1; zero-shot gpt-4o-mini fails within 25 steps.
- Limitations the authors state:
  - Alternating dual-policy optimization: Alternating updates may slightly increase overall training time because the two policies are updated in separate phases.
  - Constrained MAPPO feature selection: MAPPO-BDP requires retraining when bandwidth constraints change, which is time-consuming and energy-intensive.
  - LLM-BDP four-agent decomposition: LLM-BDP has higher inference latency and memory usage, limiting real-time use in resource-constrained settings.
- Limitations they do not state: not assessed. Results are the authors' own, from their simulations, benchmarks or surveys; none evaluates delegation to cheaper models on software work.
